section.title: Overview
section.para: On disk, /overlayer holds the layers side by side:
section.programlisting: /overlayer/ ├── syshub/ base layer: the complete operating system │ ├── bin/ sbin/ libexec/ programs │ ├── lib/ shared libraries of the primary C library │ ├── include/ headers of the primary C library │ ├── share/ architecture-independent data │ ├── etc/ system configuration │ ├── var/ variable state of base services │ ├── arch-vendor-linux-musl/ musl: loader, libc, headers, toolchain │ ├── drivers/ │ │ ├── modules/kernel/ kernel modules │ │ └── hardware/firmwares/ device firmware │ └── engine/services/ base package list, mirror list ├── zexlib/ userland layer │ ├── union/ files of installed packages │ │ └── arch-vendor-linux-gnu/ glibc, when installed │ ├── work/ OverlayFS work directory │ ├── registry/ package receipts, index, caches, keys │ └── var/ package data kept outside the union ├── zaisys/ boot layer (read-only) │ ├── kernel/ kernels and initramfs images │ └── bootloader/ boot loader files ├── agents/ instructions for AI agents (optional) └── .syshub-pending/ a staged base upgrade (only while one waits)

section.title: /overlayer/syshub: the base layer
section.para: The base layer is the complete operating system as the vendor ships it: C library, toolchain, init system, services, desktop and drivers. It MUST boot and run with the userland layer absent. It MUST be changed only by a base upgrade ().

listitem.para: Programs. sbin holds programs meant for the administrator. Both are on the default PATH.
Helper programs run by other programs, not by users.

Shared and static libraries built for the primary C library, and the data directories that FHS places under /usr/lib (for example lib/systemd, lib/udev, lib/pkgconfig). A library built for any other C library MUST NOT be placed here.
Headers for the libraries in lib. The C library's own headers are in its triplet directory, not here.
Architecture-independent data: icons, locales, manual pages, desktop files, schemas.
System configuration, including the user and group databases, name service, host names and the time zone link. Every C library on the system MUST read these files from here ().
Variable data of base services: logs, caches, spool, the state of the service manager. /var points here.
The primary C library, musl, with its loader, headers and cross-named toolchain ().
Kernel modules of each installed kernel (FHS: /lib/modules).
The list of base packages with their versions, and the list of package mirrors.

section.title: /overlayer/zexlib: the userland layer
section.para: The userland layer holds everything the user installs on top of the base. It is changed only by the package manager.

listitem.para: The files of installed packages, in the same layout as the base (bin, lib, etc, share, …). This directory is the upper layer of the system view, so its files appear in /overlayer/syshub. The secondary C library, glibc, lives in its triplet directory here ().
The OverlayFS work directory belonging to union. It MUST be on the same filesystem as union and MUST NOT be used for anything else.
One receipt per installed package listing every file it installed, the package index, download caches and trusted signing keys.
Package data that must stay outside the composed view, for example a system-wide Flatpak installation.

section.title: /overlayer/zaisys: the boot layer
section.para: The boot layer holds what is needed before the root is mounted: kernels, initramfs images and the boot loader (FHS: /boot). It is mounted read-only in the running system. On firmware that can read only FAT filesystems, the installer MAY copy the kernel and initramfs to the EFI system partition; the copies in zaisys remain the reference.
An optional directory with instructions, skills and policies for AI coding agents working on the system. Agents SHOULD read it before changing the system.

A base upgrade that has been downloaded and verified but not yet applied. It exists only while an upgrade waits for the next boot, is writable only by the package manager running as root, and MUST be applied or discarded before the system view is composed.

section.title: Documentation at the top of the hierarchy
section.para: An implementation SHOULD place a short description of the system, its architecture and its package manager directly in /overlayer, so that the layout explains itself to users and agents.
